claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start: **How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, there are some specific criteria that apply. Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19 in certain circumstances.

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar courses) or on an approved training course?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. Alex is studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know, thank you. Since Alex is 18 and studying A-levels at sixth form college, that meets the education requirement.

I have a couple more questions to determine your eligibility:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Just a couple more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex** – meaning you pay for things like food, clothes, and accommodation for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I pay for all his food, clothes, and everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. One more important question:

**Are you and Alex living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we both live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for all that information. Based on what you've told me, I have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me summarise what you've shared:
- Alex is 18 years old
- He is studying A-levels at sixth form college (approved full-time education)
- He lives with you in the UK
- You are responsible for him and pay for his food, clothes, and other needs

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm pleased to tell you that **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

✅ **Age & Education**: Although Alex is 18 (over the standard age limit of 16), Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 who remain in approved full-time education. A-levels at sixth form college counts as approved education.

✅ **Responsibility**: You are responsible for Alex as you pay for his food, clothes, and other needs.

✅ **Living arrangements**: Alex lives with you.

✅ **UK residence**: You both live in the UK.

**Please note**: Child Benefit will stop when Alex either:
- Turns 20, or
- Finishes or leaves his approved education/training, or
- Starts paid work for 24 hours or more a week and is no longer in approved education

If you'd like to proceed with your claim, you can apply through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
